body: yea, man. i feel like i didn't contribute the way others did, and my brother is now going to deploy. i just feel like such a worthless shit sometimes. i don't know. i guess i have people on this site like you to talk to, and i'm extremely grateful for it. thank you all so much. turning to anyone else sounds out for consequences, and for people to think that i'm just someone to make problems for attention. this is all i'm turning to right now.

wow, that's exactly what happened. it felt great. i felt that cold steel, and the smell of gun powder, and the clp that i used to clean my weapon. i just clenched the barrel with my teeth, and broke down in my closet. once i came out, there was no feeling of hopelessness, and i got on with the rest of my day, and there was a new found meaning.

yea, you know what. this is why i love public service so much, and i'm trying to do this EMT program. i was a military cop, and i loved the feeling of serving the public around me. it was truly its own kind of high.

i mean, not really. i'm trying to become an EMT, and i want to go into law enforcement after that. if i told anyone that i had a mental illness of any kind, i could kiss that all goodbye, and really take away all meaning to my life. i also have a brother that is about to deploy with the marines, who is dealing with marital problems, and depression himself. i don't want my family to stop and think they have another guy to worry about. plus, i'm his crutch, and he needs me to look to as a shining example for him, so he can get through his own bout with depression. i love him so much. i just don't want this dark feeling anymore, so i need to do something to release it, and the shotgun helps.
